core: real, pictorial, positive, and negative space
outOfScope: claims of one universally correct depth system

claims.claim: Real space is three-dimensional, while a work's space can also refer to the area of a picture plane and an image's feeling of depth.
Positive space is commonly the area occupied by primary objects and negative space is the surrounding area.
Perspective drawing and shading can create an illusion of three-dimensional space in a two-dimensional work.
Atmospheric changes and linear perspective can be used as visible depth cues in pictorial space.
Formal analysis can describe spatial organization and viewpoint but needs other evidence for claims about intention, historical meaning, or audience response.
A photograph records one framing and viewpoint rather than every possible encounter with a three-dimensional artwork or installation.
